candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos II.23
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.23 (c. 350 AD)

'And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever' — Athanasius marks pan ktisma (every creature) worshiping tō kathēmenō epi tō thronō kai tō arniō (the-One-sitting upon the throne AND the Lamb) as the cosmic-Apocalyptic-divinity confession. The verse explicitly-distinguishes the Lamb (the incarnate-Christ) from pan-ktisma (every-creature) — the Lamb is therefore-NOT among-the-creatures, but stands with the Father-on-the-throne as the joint-recipient of cosmic-creaturely-worship. The four-fold doxology (eulogia + timē + doxa + kratos — blessing + honor + glory + power) is offered indistinguishably to Father-and-Lamb, marking ontological-equality. The Tewahedo Anaphora doxological-section cites Rev 5:13 + 7:10 + 11:15 as the apocalyptic-divinity-triad.

candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §20 (c. 350 AD)

'And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation' — Athanasius marks axios ei labein to biblion... hoti esphagēs kai ēgorasas tō theō en tō haimati sou (thou art WORTHY to take the book... for thou wast slain and hast purchased to God by thy blood) as the APOCALYPTIC REDEMPTION-BY-BLOOD anchor. The worthiness (axios) is HYPER-CREATURELY: only the divine-incarnate could redeem the cosmos. The ēgorasas (purchased / redeemed) is commercial-language: the Word's-blood is the redemption-price. The ek pasēs phylēs kai glōssēs (out of every tribe and tongue) marks the cosmic-scope: the redemption is for all-humanity, not Israel-only. Tewahedo Anaphora cites Rev 5:9 at the Communion-distribution as the universal-redemption-by-blood acclamation.
